title.en: Default numeric tolerance rule for checks

summary: Give every numeric check a default tolerance and regime so a comparison can fail on its own instead of asking the author to invent one.
objective: Apply a stated default tolerance to any numeric check that does not declare its own, and record the tolerance and regime beside the result.
intent_signals: Choose a tolerance for a numeric check.
Decide how close is close enough when comparing a computed value with an expected one.
example_prompts: Give the default tolerance for comparing a computed position with its analytic value.
State a pass criterion for a check that only says the values should agree.

principles: A check without a number is not a check: a comparison that delegates its tolerance to the reader can never report a failure by itself.
Separate the three failure sources a tolerance has to absorb: floating-point roundoff, the discretisation or model regime, and genuine modelling error. Only the first two justify a loose bound.
Scale absolute tolerances to the quantity being compared. Positions scale with the scene, angles do not, and counts, indices and permutations are exact and must not be given a tolerance at all.
A tolerance is meaningless without its regime. Small-angle, fixed-step, linearised and far-field approximations all move the residual by orders of magnitude, so the regime travels with the number.
implementation: Use these defaults when a record does not state its own: relative tolerance rtol = 1e-6; absolute position tolerance atol_position = 1e-9 x scene_scale_m; angular tolerance 1e-6 rad; integer or discrete state compared exactly; a sampled period accepted to within one sample; and a visual comparison given an explicit pixel or percent threshold rather than an opinion.
Declare scene_scale_m once per scene as the largest modelled dimension in metres, and derive atol_position from it, so a millimetre model and a kilometre terrain do not share one absolute bound.
Combine the two forms as |computed - expected| <= atol + rtol x |expected| rather than choosing one, so the check survives an expected value near zero.

Override the defaults deliberately, in the record that needs it, with the reason attached: a first-order integrator, a truncated series or a coarse mesh needs a bound derived from its step or order, not a looser round number.
Report the tolerance actually used and the regime it assumes next to every numeric result, including passes; a pass with an undisclosed tolerance carries no information.
observable_checks: Every numeric check in the record names either these defaults or its own tolerance, and no check text asks the reader to supply one.
Deliberately perturbing the compared quantity by slightly more than the stated tolerance makes the check fail, and by slightly less makes it pass.
Exact quantities (piece permutations, site counts, discrete branch labels, integer state) are compared with equality and report no tolerance.

defaults.rationale: Authored engineering defaults, not measurements and not a claim about any implementation. rtol = 1e-6 sits far above double-precision roundoff for well-conditioned arithmetic while staying tight enough that a real modelling error shows; atol_position is expressed as a fraction of scene scale so it transfers between a millimetre model and a kilometre terrain; sampled quantities cannot be resolved better than the sampling interval, so one sample is the floor; visual comparisons get a stated threshold because an unstated one cannot fail. These values assume double precision and a declared regime, and any record with a coarser integrator, a truncated series or a stated approximation should override them with a bound derived from its own step or order.

values.visual: state a pixel or percent threshold explicitly
values.regime_note: double precision; declare the regime (e.g. small-angle) when the model is approximate

known_limits: These are default starting bounds for authored checks, not a numerical-accuracy guarantee and not a substitute for an error analysis of a particular scheme.

A record whose model is approximate, whose integrator is low order or whose inputs are ill-conditioned will need a looser and separately justified bound; applying the defaults there produces false failures.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact or improvement has been observed for this record.
creative_affordances: State tolerances in whatever units and presentation the scene already uses, as long as the number and its regime are both visible.
